# tau spine

The spine of a tau (0.1.0+2399d92df219): a Cloudflare Worker whose hostname is the tau's address. It
serves the tau's public card at `/.well-known/tau.json`, keeps the sealed envelopes other
taus send until the hub picks them up, and gives the hub its API under `/hub/*`. It never
decrypts anything and holds no contacts. It runs in local mode and fits the Workers Free plan.

This directory was written by `tau net spine init` from the kit inside the `tau-net` Python
package. You do not need the tau repository.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `worker.js` | the bundled Worker; deployed as it is |
| `wrangler.jsonc` | its Wrangler configuration (name `tau-spine`, bindings, cron) |
| `package.json` | Wrangler, pinned |

## Deploy

Requirements: Node.js 22 or newer and a Cloudflare account (the Free plan is enough).

```sh
npx wrangler login               # once
tau net spine deploy <this directory>
```

`tau net spine deploy` installs Wrangler, deploys the Worker,
creates `TAU_SPINE_TOKEN` in the hub's `.env` when it is missing, sets it as the Worker's
`HUB_TOKEN` secret and writes `TAU_SPINE_URL`. Then, on the hub:

```sh
tau net init --name "Alice's tau"
tau net publish
tau net status
```

By hand, the same steps are:

```sh
npm install
npx wrangler deploy
npx wrangler secret put HUB_TOKEN   # the hub's TAU_SPINE_TOKEN
```

The first deploy provisions the storage the Worker needs in your account. The address is
`tau-spine.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev`, or your own domain when `vars.ADDRESS` and
`routes` are set in `wrangler.jsonc` (`tau net spine init --address HOST` does that; the
zone must be on your Cloudflare account). Contacts know your tau by its address, so choose it
before you add any.

## Update

Upgrade `tau-net`, run `tau net spine init` into a new directory, and deploy that one. The
Worker name `tau-spine` stays the same, so the new version replaces the old one, and
bindings without an id keep the storage the deployed Worker already uses.
